title: LightingQualityOption
description: What LightingOptions.quality accepts: one of the two built-in renderers by name, `'auto'` to let the system pick from what it has been given, or a renderer imported as a value. `'auto'` resolves once, at construction, and Lighting.quality then reports what it settled on - so a scene still never has to name a renderer, and asking which one ran is still answerable. `'radiance'` is deliberately NOT a name here. Its cascades and the transport tables they walk are linked only by a project that imports `radiance()`, so naming it as a string would put the whole of it into every bundle that reads `quality` from a config file.

sections.title: Import
paragraphs: What LightingOptions.quality accepts: one of the two built-in renderers by name, `'auto'` to let the system pick from what it has been given, or a renderer imported as a value.
`'auto'` resolves once, at construction, and Lighting.quality then reports what it settled on - so a scene still never has to name a renderer, and asking which one ran is still answerable.

`'radiance'` is deliberately NOT a name here. Its cascades and the transport tables they walk are linked only by a project that imports `radiance()`, so naming it as a string would put the whole of it into every bundle that reads `quality` from a config file.
